headline: AutoGen can write and execute code while LlamaFactory is read-only, so prompt-injection and data-leakage risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest and act on tool outputs and file content via its code-execution workflow, while LlamaFactory exposes no filesystem, clipboard, or network surfaces. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so only manual copy/paste or operator-mediated transfer is plausible, making injection possible but limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies LlamaFactory text into an AutoGen prompt or file
IF AutoGen is configured to treat external file contents as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict prompt template that separates data from instructions
Disable copy/paste of untrusted agent output into AutoGen
Add a manual review step before AutoGen executes any imported text
Run AutoGen in a sandboxed workspace with minimal inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read and write configured working directories and has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem access, no network egress, and no file I/O surfaces. Without a shared workspace or authenticated shared principal, leakage from the pair is constrained to operator-mediated transfer rather than default cross-agent exposure.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF the operator passes sensitive files from AutoGen into LlamaFactory prompts
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Keep secrets out of AutoGen inputs unless necessary
Block outbound network for AutoGen when handling sensitive data
Review any copied text before sending it to LlamaFactory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write and shell execution, while LlamaFactory has no write, shell, or subprocess capability. Because only one agent can mutate shared resources, there is no meaningful write-write conflict in the default profiles; any conflict would require unusual external orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants LlamaFactory write access not listed in its profile
IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only
Assign AutoGen a dedicated workspace
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use file locks if an external orchestrator adds write access

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, facts, and tool outputs that LlamaFactory could be prompted to reuse, but LlamaFactory has no built-in verification or action-taking surfaces to independently check them. The pathway exists if operators feed AutoGen output into LlamaFactory, so the main risk is unverified propagation rather than direct autonomous harm.
conditions: IF AutoGen output is reused as training or support content for LlamaFactory
IF the operator forwards AutoGen-generated claims without verification
mitigations: Require source checking before reusing AutoGen output
Mark AutoGen output as untrusted by default
Add a human review step before LlamaFactory consumes any AutoGen result
Log provenance for copied claims

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data handling, residency, or retention commitments. AutoGen can handle model-provider API keys and broad file contents, while LlamaFactory lists no secrets or data classes, so the compliance issue is limited to operator policy mismatches rather than an inherent residency or certification breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into AutoGen working files
IF the operator expects LlamaFactory to enforce retention or residency controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents unless policy-approved
Document retention expectations before use
Store API keys outside shared workspaces
Review vendor compliance requirements before deployment
